key_insight: Real coding-agent workloads are dominated by long autonomous, tool-heavy loops with long contexts, short outputs, and strong but imperfect cache reuse.
engineering_relevance: Serving systems for coding agents should optimize tool-call overhead, prefill for append-heavy contexts, latency prediction, and KV-cache retention across human-paced gaps.
method: Collected ~4,300 real daily coding-agent sessions from Claude Code and Codex
Captured ~350,000 LLM steps and ~430,000 tool calls
Analyzed workload patterns to identify serving bottlenecks and optimization opportunities
evidence_signal: The trace provides large-scale real-world evidence from day-to-day use, spanning multiple agent and model families, rather than synthetic benchmarks.
watch_item: Results come from the authors' own usage traces, so workload patterns may reflect their environment, tools, and coding style rather than all agent deployments.
paper_title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
